summary: Backend-only verification of new Subscription (recurring booking) module. Wrote pytest suite at /app/backend/tests/test_subscription_module.py with 12 test functions covering: admin catalog service creation with is_subscription+subscription_plans, plan preview financials, subscription creation with schedule + immutable snapshot (commission/tax/allocation/per_day_earning), snapshot immutability after admin PUT /api/admin/settings commission change, mock upfront payment activation, admin partners list + assign, partner day complete + weekly_off rejection + non-assigned 403, admin maid_absent/customer_cancel (neutral)/weekly_off protection/replacement_completed accrual, full 10000/26/20% money reconciliation (accrued=24*per_day ~7384.62, absent_adjustment=2*per_day ~615.38, sum=8000 partner_allocation), finalize -> pending -> pay-before-approve rejected -> review -> approve -> pay credits partner wallet by exact settlement amount, listing endpoints (mine, partner/mine, admin/all, admin/stats), and regression non-subscription catalog create. All 12/12 passed in 12.2s.
critical_code_review_comments: subscription_service.plan_preview uses _parse_ref() (today) to count working_days when plan.working_days is falsy; if the customer picks a start_date whose week alignment differs from today, the previewed per_day_earning can drift from the actual booking. Preview is decoupled from create (create counts working_days from the schedule built with the actual start_date), so numbers on the review screen may not exactly match the created subscription for auto-computed working_days. Explicit plan.working_days (as used in tests) avoids this. Consider taking start_date into preview or documenting the caveat.

controllers/subscription_controller._set_day allows overriding an already-completed day back to any other status (e.g., completed -> maid_absent) because allowed_from is only enforced on the partner path. Consider guarding against silently changing days already marked completed/absent via admin to keep the audit trail intact (or explicitly document it as an admin override).

pay_settlement is idempotent for the assigned partner (short-circuits if settlement.status==paid) but the replacement-earnings loop runs BEFORE that gate on the first call only; if a caller ever hits pay twice concurrently there is a minor race window. In practice guarded by admin approve->pay flow.
SettingsUpdate model does not include `payment` config field; unrelated to this module but note that some settings paths use nested dicts. Not a blocker.
